certificate.title: Module 3: Using AI to Analyze, Review & Validate Completion

course.description: Use AI as your analyst and quality checker. Review contracts, reconciliations, journal entries, and financial documents with a second set of eyes that never gets tired. Turn one-time reviews into reusable checklists. Build a Finance Review Analyst agent.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Module 3: Using AI to Analyze, Review & Validate.

modules.description: How AI reads documents — without getting tired or losing focus. Why it's the second set of eyes your team always needed.

activities.title: What AI Is Good At: Finding Things You Might Miss

lessons.content:
Finance professionals spend a significant amount of time reviewing things — contracts, reconciliations, journal entries, reports, policies, data. This review work is critical, but it's also where errors hide. When you're reviewing a 30-page contract or a spreadsheet with 500 rows, your attention isn't uniform. You're sharp on page 1, less sharp on page 22. You catch the big things but miss the subtle inconsistencies.

AI doesn't have this problem. It reads every line with the same level of attention. It can cross-reference a number on page 3 with a number on page 27. It can spot when a contract says "net 30" in one section and "net 45" in another. It's not smarter than you — but it's more consistent.
lessons.title: What AI Is Good At: Finding Things You Might Miss

activities.title: The "Second Set of Eyes" You Always Wanted

lessons.content:
Think about how review works in most finance teams:

| Traditional Review | AI-Assisted Review |
|---|---|
| You review it yourself, hoping you catch everything | AI reviews it first, flags potential issues, then you review the flags |
| You ask a colleague to review — but they're busy | AI is always available and never too busy |
| You re-read the same document three times | AI reads it once and gives you a structured summary of what to look at |
| You check numbers manually, cell by cell | AI cross-references numbers across the document in seconds |

AI doesn't replace your judgment. It does the tedious scanning so you can focus your expertise on the things that actually need human decision-making.
lessons.title: The "Second Set of Eyes" You Always Wanted

activities.title: What You Can Analyze and Review

lessons.content:
The range is broader than you might think:

**Documents and Contracts**
- Vendor contracts, lease agreements, SOWs
- Board resolutions, policy documents
- Audit reports, management letters

**Financial Data**
- Account reconciliations
- Journal entry support
- Budget vs. actual comparisons
- Intercompany transaction logs

**Reports and Outputs**
- Financial statements for internal consistency
- Management reports for accuracy and clarity
- Presentation decks for numerical accuracy

**Processes and Controls**
- Process documentation for gaps
- Control descriptions for completeness
- Checklists for coverage
lessons.title: What You Can Analyze and Review

activities.title: Choose Your Scenario

lessons.content:
Pick something real from your work that needs analysis or review — a spreadsheet, a contract, a report, a reconciliation, or any work product that benefits from a second set of eyes.

**The default example used throughout this module is:**

> **Reviewing a vendor contract** — checking terms, identifying risks, flagging items that need finance's attention before signing.

If you don't have a document handy, no problem — you can ask AI to generate a sample for practice (Step 2 shows you how).
lessons.title: Choose Your Scenario

modules.title: Context / Theory

modules.description: Hands-on steps. Generate a sample contract, have AI review it critically, go deeper on specific findings, and turn the review into a reusable checklist.

activities.title: Step 1: Open an AI Tool

lessons.content:
Go to one of the platforms below and sign in.

- **ChatGPT** → https://chat.openai.com
- **Claude** → https://claude.ai
- **Grok** → https://grok.com

**Note:** For this module, it's helpful to have a document to work with — a PDF, a spreadsheet export, or text you can paste. If you don't have one handy, Step 2 shows you how to ask AI to generate a sample.
lessons.title: Step 1: Open an AI Tool

activities.title: Step 2: Give AI Something to Review

lessons.content:
**Option A: Use a real document.** Paste it in (or upload it if the platform supports file uploads). Remove any truly confidential information first — client names, bank account numbers, etc.

**Option B: Ask AI to generate a sample.** If you don't have a document handy:

> **Try this (default example):**
> "Generate a realistic sample vendor contract for a SaaS platform that a finance team would need to review. Include payment terms, auto-renewal clauses, termination provisions, liability caps, data security provisions, and SLA commitments. Make it about 3 pages long and include a few subtle issues that a careful reviewer might catch — like inconsistent payment terms or a missing data deletion clause."

AI will generate a realistic contract. Now you have something to work with.
lessons.title: Step 2: Give AI Something to Review

activities.title: Step 3: Ask AI to Review It

lessons.content:
Ask AI to review the document critically. Be specific about what you're looking for.

> **Try this (default example):**
> "Review this vendor contract from a finance perspective. I need you to:
> 1. Summarize the key commercial terms (pricing, payment terms, contract length, renewal)
> 2. Flag any risks or unfavorable terms
> 3. Identify any inconsistencies within the document
> 4. Note anything that's missing that should be in a contract like this
> 5. Give me a list of questions I should ask the vendor before signing"

Read the response. Notice how AI structured its review — organized findings into categories, highlighted specific clauses, and gave you actionable items. This is the kind of review that would take 30-60 minutes to do manually.
lessons.title: Step 3: Ask AI to Review It

activities.title: Step 4: Go Deeper on Specific Issues

lessons.content:
When AI flags something, don't stop there. Ask follow-up questions to understand the implications:

| You Ask | Why |
|---|---|
| "The auto-renewal clause — what's standard in the industry? Is 60-day notice reasonable?" | Benchmark against norms |
| "You mentioned the liability cap is low. What would a reasonable cap look like for a contract this size?" | Get specific guidance |
| "Can you rewrite clause 7.2 to be more favorable to us as the buyer?" | Get suggested language |
| "Compare the data security provisions to what SOC 2 would require" | Validate against a standard |
| "What's the financial exposure if we need to terminate early under these terms?" | Quantify the risk |

This is where AI becomes a true analyst — it doesn't just flag issues, it helps you understand them, quantify them, and decide what to do.
lessons.title: Step 4: Go Deeper on Specific Issues

activities.title: Step 5: Try a Different Type of Review

lessons.content:
Now try a different analysis task closer to your day-to-day work:

**Reconciliation review:**
> "Here's a bank reconciliation for our operating account [paste or describe the data]. Check for: (1) any timing differences older than 30 days, (2) any items over $10K that need investigation, (3) whether the ending balance ties. Flag anything that looks unusual."

**Financial statement consistency check:**
> "I'm going to give you our Q3 income statement and balance sheet. Check whether: (1) net income on the P&L matches the change in retained earnings, (2) depreciation expense is consistent with the change in accumulated depreciation, (3) any line items show unusual swings from the prior quarter."

**Journal entry review:**
> "Here are the top 20 journal entries by dollar amount for the month. Review them for: (1) entries without adequate descriptions, (2) unusual account combinations, (3) round-dollar amounts above $50K that might be estimates, (4) any entries that debit and credit the same account."
lessons.title: Step 5: Try a Different Type of Review

activities.title: Step 6: Create a Checklist from Your Review

lessons.content:
One of the most powerful things you can do after a review is turn it into a reusable checklist. Ask AI:

> "Based on the contract review we just did, create a reusable checklist I can use every time I need to review a vendor contract. Organize it by category (commercial terms, legal risk, data/security, operational) and make each item a yes/no question I can check off."

Now you have a review tool — not just a one-time analysis, but a repeatable process. Save this checklist. You'll use it again.
lessons.title: Step 6: Create a Checklist from Your Review

activities.title: Step 7: Reflect

lessons.content:
You just used AI to analyze and review work. Think about the experience:

- How did it compare to doing the review yourself? Did AI catch things you might have missed?
- How much faster was the first pass with AI vs. doing it manually?
- Did AI flag anything that seemed wrong or off-base?
- How would you use this in your current review processes — as a first pass? As a quality check on your own review?

Important caveat: for critical reviews — compliance matters, external filings, significant contracts — AI should be your first pass, not your only pass. Your professional judgment is still the final checkpoint. But by the time you get to your review, AI has already done the heavy lifting.
lessons.title: Step 7: Reflect

modules.title: Now To Do

modules.description: Every type of review task AI can assist with — contracts, reconciliations, journal entries, policies, and audit prep.

activities.title: Contract and Document Review

lessons.content:
- **Vendor contracts:** Before signing any vendor agreement, run it through AI to flag unfavorable terms, missing clauses, and financial risks. You'll walk into the negotiation knowing exactly what to push back on.

- **Lease agreements:** When reviewing leases under ASC 842, have AI extract the key terms (commencement date, term, options, payments, escalations) and flag any embedded lease components.

- **SOWs and amendments:** Statements of work often have inconsistencies with the master agreement. AI can compare the two and highlight conflicts.

- **Insurance policies:** Annual insurance renewals come with dense policy documents. AI can summarize coverage, flag exclusions, and compare against prior year terms.
lessons.title: Contract and Document Review

activities.title: Financial Review and Quality Control

lessons.content:
- **Account reconciliations:** Have AI review reconciliations for stale items, unusual entries, and items that don't tie. It's a faster first-pass than reviewing line by line.

- **Journal entry testing:** Upload a list of journal entries and have AI flag unusual patterns — entries without descriptions, unusual account combinations, entries posted at odd times, round-dollar estimates.

- **Intercompany balances:** Cross-reference IC balances across entities and flag mismatches, timing differences, and unreconciled amounts.

- **Financial statement review:** Before issuing financials, have AI check internal consistency — does the balance sheet balance? Does the cash flow statement reconcile? Do footnotes match the face of the statements?
lessons.title: Financial Review and Quality Control

activities.title: Compliance, Policy, and Audit Preparation

lessons.content:
**Compliance and Policy:**
- **SOX control documentation:** Review control descriptions for completeness — does each control have a clear objective, frequency, performer, evidence, and what-can-go-wrong scenario?
- **Policy documents:** When updating policies, have AI review for gaps, ambiguities, and internal contradictions.
- **Regulatory filings:** Before submitting filings, have AI review for completeness against the checklist of required disclosures.

**Audit Preparation:**
- **Pre-audit review:** Before external auditors arrive, run your own AI-assisted review of the areas they'll test. Find and fix issues before they do.
- **PBC list preparation:** When auditors send their prepared-by-client list, use AI to help organize your response and check that every item is addressed.
- **Prior year findings:** Give AI last year's management letter and ask it to verify that every finding has been remediated.
lessons.title: Compliance, Policy, and Audit Preparation

modules.title: Application

modules.description: Optional. Build a Finance Review Analyst agent with your standards and checklists built in — ready to review any document you hand it.

activities.title: The Idea: A Reviewer That Already Knows Your Standards

lessons.content:
In the main exercise, you gave AI ad hoc review instructions each time. That works for one-off analyses. But for review tasks you do regularly — contract reviews, recon reviews, journal entry testing — you can create a **review agent** that already knows your standards, your checklists, and what to look for. Open it up, paste the document, and it immediately knows how to review it.

**What you'll create:** A Finance Review Analyst — an AI assistant specialized in analyzing, reviewing, and validating documents and data against your specific criteria.
lessons.title: The Idea: A Reviewer That Already Knows Your Standards

activities.title: Option A: Create a Custom GPT in ChatGPT

lessons.content:
1. Go to **https://chat.openai.com** and sign in
2. In the sidebar, click **Explore GPTs** → **Create**
3. **Name:** `Finance Review Analyst`
4. **Instructions:** Paste the following (modify for your role):

```
You are my dedicated review and analysis agent. I work in a finance function and need help reviewing documents, data, and work products critically and thoroughly.

When I give you something to review:
- Start with a brief summary of what you're looking at
- Organize your findings into clear categories (e.g., commercial terms, risks, inconsistencies, missing items)
- For each finding, explain WHY it matters — not just what you found, but what the impact or risk is
- Prioritize findings: flag critical issues separately from nice-to-haves
- End with a clear list of recommended actions or questions to raise
- If I ask you to cross-reference or validate numbers, show your work

My review standards:
- Contracts: check payment terms, renewal/termination clauses, liability, data security, SLAs, and anything non-standard
- Reconciliations: flag items over 30 days old, amounts over $10K, and anything that doesn't tie
- Journal entries: flag missing descriptions, unusual account combinations, round-dollar estimates, and entries over $50K
- Policies: check for gaps, ambiguities, contradictions, and missing best practices

Always be thorough but practical. I need findings I can act on, not academic observations.
```

5. Click **Save** → Choose **Only me**
lessons.title: Option A: Create a Custom GPT in ChatGPT

activities.title: Option B: Create a Project in Claude

lessons.content:
1. Go to **https://claude.ai** and sign in
2. In the sidebar, click **Projects** → **Create a project**
3. **Name:** `Finance Review Analyst`
4. In the **Project instructions** field, paste the same instructions from Option A
5. Click **Create project**
lessons.title: Option B: Create a Project in Claude

activities.title: Option C: Create an Agent in AI Gym

lessons.content:
1. Open the **AI Gym** app and sign in (download at https://aigym.studio/#download if needed)
2. On Home, type: *"Create an agent called Finance Review Analyst in my My Training Portfolio org with these instructions:"* and paste the instructions from Option A
3. The Hub creates it for you. Or go to **Org** → My Training Portfolio → **+ New Agent**

Your review agent is now part of your training portfolio alongside your research and communications agents.
lessons.title: Option C: Create an Agent in AI Gym

activities.title: Build on Your Portfolio

lessons.content:
Open a conversation with your **Using AI Series Agent** and update it:

> "I just completed Module 3. I created a Finance Review Analyst agent. I learned how to use AI to review contracts, reconciliations, and financial documents — and how to turn findings into reusable checklists. The biggest takeaway was [your takeaway]."

Your portfolio now has **three working agents**: a research expert, a communications writer, and a review analyst.
lessons.title: Build on Your Portfolio

modules.title: Bonus: Going Deeper

modules.description: Key terms introduced in this module, explained in plain language.

activities.title: Cross-referencing

lessons.content: When AI checks one part of a document against another — like verifying that a number on page 3 matches a number on page 27, or that payment terms in the body match the terms in the summary. This is one of AI's strengths: it reads the entire document at once and can spot inconsistencies humans miss.
lessons.title: Cross-referencing

activities.title: Structured Output

lessons.content: When AI organizes its response in a specific format — like a table, a categorized list, or a checklist. You can ask for structured output explicitly: "Give me a table," "Organize by priority," "Make it a checklist." This makes AI output immediately usable rather than just informational.
lessons.title: Structured Output

activities.title: First Pass / Second Pass

lessons.content: A review approach where AI does the first pass (scanning for issues, flagging findings) and you do the second pass (evaluating the flags, making decisions). This is the most practical way to integrate AI into review workflows — it catches the obvious things so you can focus on the nuanced ones.
lessons.title: First Pass / Second Pass

activities.title: Validation

lessons.content: Checking that something is correct, complete, and consistent. AI can validate numbers (do they add up?), documents (are all required sections present?), and logic (does this conclusion follow from this data?). Validation is different from creation — you're not asking AI to make something new, you're asking it to check something that exists.
lessons.title: Validation

activities.title: Upload / File Input

lessons.content: Some AI platforms (ChatGPT, Claude) let you upload files directly — PDFs, spreadsheets, images. This is especially useful for review tasks where you need AI to work with an actual document rather than pasted text. Check your platform's capabilities for supported file types.
lessons.title: Upload / File Input
